title: Emergency Housing Vouchers: Owner Incentives and the 2035 Wind-Down
metaDescription: Emergency Housing Voucher landlord incentives in Cleveland: what CMHA's plan allows and what HUD's EHV renewal cutoff means for a lease you sign now.
primaryKeyword: emergency housing voucher landlord incentive cleveland
answerBox: CMHA's Administrative Plan authorizes owner incentive or retention payments for Emergency Housing Voucher lease-ups, but publishes no dollar amount — the payment is discretionary. Separately, HUD will issue no further EHV renewal funding, yet any remaining EHV funds do not expire until September 30, 2035. Confirm details with CMHA.

sections.h2: What CMHA can offer on an Emergency Housing Voucher lease
body: Here is the honest version. CMHA's Administrative Plan **authorizes** owner incentive and retention payments tied to Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) lease-ups, but it does not promise a specific dollar amount. The plan's language is permissive: "The PHA may make incentive or retention payments to owners that agree to initially lease their unit to an EHV family and/or renew the lease of an EHV family." That payment is made as a single payment at the start of the lease term, and it is **not counted as rent or in rent reasonableness** — so it sits on top of the approved rent rather than reducing it.

Two things follow from that word "may." First, there is no published EHV signing figure to quote, so treat any specific dollar promise you see online with suspicion — especially numbers attached to the Columbus housing authority, a different agency that shares the CMHA acronym. Second, whether an incentive applies to your specific EHV lease is a question only CMHA can answer, so ask before you count on it.

sections.h2: How this differs from ordinary voucher incentives in Cuyahoga County
body: For a standard Housing Choice Voucher tenancy, CMHA itself publishes **no** general signing bonus, damage-mitigation fund, or vacancy-loss payment — none appears in its Landlord FAQ, its Leasing with CMHA page, or its landlord newsletters. The local incentives that do carry real dollar amounts belong to the **Cuyahoga Community Choice Demonstration**, not to CMHA across the board: that program advertises a lease-up bonus and a Damage Mitigation Fund of up to $2,000, but only when the tenant is a Community Choice client renting a unit in a designated Opportunity Area.

If your unit might qualify, that is a separate track — confirm eligibility with the Community Choice Demonstration directly before you count on it. For the full picture of who actually cuts a check to a Cleveland voucher landlord, see [who pays landlords under CMHA, EDEN and CoC](/who-pays-landlords-cmha-eden-coc-cleveland/).

sections.h2: What HUD ending EHV renewal funding means for a lease you sign now
body: This is the part that makes owners nervous, and it deserves a straight answer. In a **March 6, 2025** letter to PHA Executive Directors, HUD stated that after its final Emergency Housing Voucher allocation, "the Department will provide no additional EHV CY HAP Renewal funding allocations to PHAs." In plain terms: EHV is a closed program that HUD is not topping up indefinitely.

But "no more renewal funding" is not the same as "the money stops next year." The same guidance is explicit that any remaining Emergency Housing Voucher funds **do not expire until September 30, 2035**. That is close to a decade of runway from today. A one-year lease you sign now — or several consecutive renewals — sits comfortably inside that window, funded by dollars that are already committed rather than dependent on a fresh appropriation each year.

One caution: we cannot give you a local Cuyahoga County EHV wind-down date, because CMHA has not published one. If you find a "June 2026" EHV cutoff online, check the source — a cutoff by that date was published by a housing agency in Georgia and has nothing to do with Cleveland. Do not plan around another state's calendar. The federal outer limit is September 30, 2035; anything more specific for Cuyahoga should come from CMHA directly.

sections.h2: Questions to put to CMHA before you sign an EHV tenancy
body: EHV is one of several special federal voucher streams. CMHA confirms it administers HUD-VASH for veterans — see our [HUD-VASH landlord guide](/hud-vash-landlord-guide-cleveland/) — but for others, including [Mainstream vouchers](/mainstream-voucher-landlord-guide-cleveland/) and EHV, its public program pages do not confirm current operation. So confirm, in writing, before you rely on any of them. Specifically ask:

items: Whether CMHA is currently placing EHV families, and whether an EHV tenancy is realistically on the table for your unit — its public program pages do not confirm an active EHV pipeline or a voucher count, so do not trust unsourced totals you find online.
Whether CMHA will make an incentive or retention payment on your lease, and, if so, the amount and timing.
CMHA's own local EHV wind-down timeline, beyond the federal September 30, 2035 fund-expiration date.
Whether the payment standard and rent-reasonableness review work any differently for an EHV unit than for a standard voucher.

sections.h2: The lease-up mechanics — and where we take the work off your plate
body: An EHV placement is a **new tenancy**, which means it runs through CMHA's standard lease-up path. Since **January 1, 2026**, submitting a Request for Tenancy Approval (RFTA) triggers a requirement that the owner or designated managing agent complete CMHA's **Virtual Landlord Orientation** — required once every 24 months — and that orientation must be finished **before CMHA can execute a HAP contract for a new tenancy**. Existing HAP contracts and current payments are not affected. The session is a live, roughly 90-minute virtual class registered through Eventbrite.

We have already completed CMHA's Virtual Landlord Orientation, so an EHV lease-up handled through us is not held up waiting on that step. From there the usual rules apply: CMHA will not execute the HAP contract until you submit an IRS Form W-9, the contract must be executed within 60 calendar days of the lease start or it is void, and all owners must receive HAP by mandatory direct deposit.

Our terms are simple. Tenant placement is **one month's rent, charged only after the tenant is placed** — no placement, no fee. We will attend the CMHA inspection and send you a written report for **$100**, or you can attend yourself. Ongoing management is **5% of monthly rent, only while the unit is rented**. Repair estimates are free, itemized, and back to you within 24 hours, and nothing starts without your approval. sections.h2: A quick word on your right to say no
body: In the **City of Cleveland**, source of income is not a protected class, so an owner there may lawfully decline a voucher — this article is about why an EHV tenancy can be worth it, never a claim that you must accept one. Local ordinances do vary: Cleveland Heights, for example, prohibits source-of-income discrimination, and its Fair Practices Board can seek injunctive relief, actual damages, civil penalties up to $10,000, and reasonable attorney's fees. Know the rule where your unit sits before you decide.

faq.q: Does CMHA guarantee an incentive payment for an EHV lease?
faq.a: No. CMHA's Administrative Plan says the authority "may" make incentive or retention payments to EHV owners — it is discretionary, and no dollar amount is published. Any specific figure you see online should be verified with CMHA, and watch for numbers that actually belong to the Columbus housing authority, a different agency that shares the acronym.

faq.q: Will EHV funding run out before my lease ends?
faq.a: HUD will issue no further EHV renewal allocations, but any remaining EHV funds do not expire until September 30, 2035 — nearly a decade of committed runway. CMHA has not published a local Cuyahoga cutoff, so confirm its timeline directly and ignore cutoff dates published by housing agencies in other states.

faq.q: Does CMHA operate an EHV program in Cuyahoga County?
faq.a: Its Administrative Plan includes an EHV incentive provision, but CMHA's public program pages do not confirm an active EHV pipeline or a voucher count. Do not rely on unsourced totals you find online. Ask CMHA directly whether it is currently placing EHV families and whether your unit could host one.

faq.q: Is the EHV incentive treated as extra rent?
faq.a: No. The Administrative Plan states the payment is made as a single payment at the start of the lease term and is not counted as rent or in rent reasonableness — so it does not lower the rent CMHA will approve for the unit. It is intended to sit on top of the approved rent.

faq.q: Do I need CMHA's landlord orientation for an EHV lease-up?
faq.a: Yes, for a new tenancy. Since January 1, 2026, submitting an RFTA requires the owner or managing agent to complete CMHA's Virtual Landlord Orientation before CMHA can execute the HAP contract; existing contracts and payments are unaffected. We have already completed the orientation, so it will not hold up your lease-up.
